Live-action, photorealistic, cinematic film footage — not animation, not CGI-stylized, not cartoon.

[0 to 5s] A man in his early 30s sits across a small wooden table from a woman in a dimly lit café, warm tungsten light spilling from a lamp beside them, rain streaking the window in the background. He leans forward slightly, hands wrapped around a coffee cup, and speaks quietly: "I should have told you sooner. I just didn't know how." Natural skin texture, subtle emotion in his eyes, soft shallow depth of field with the background gently out of focus. Camera holds a static medium close-up on him.

[5 to 10s] Camera cuts to a matching medium close-up on the woman, her expression shifting from hurt to quiet understanding as she listens. She looks down at her cup, then back up at him, and responds softly: "I just wish I'd heard it from you first." Same warm lighting and shallow depth of field, natural film grain, subtle handheld micro-movement as if a real camera operator is holding the shot.

Sound: soft rain against glass, quiet café ambience, ceramic cup set down gently, two natural speaking voices with realistic room tone — no music.

[4s-5s] Final card "DIRECTED BY COMFYUI" holds, one VHS tracking glitch settling into stability.
